source.title: Analyzing Neural Scaling Laws in Two-Layer Networks with Power-Law Data Spectra

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests scaling behavior in a two-layer student-teacher setting, including an image-dataset application, rather than language-model pretraining.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own results on generalization error in one-pass SGD. Statements about prior empirical language-model scaling laws in the introduction and cited works are not this study's results. The reported measure is squared-loss generalization error, not held-out language-model cross-entropy.
record.test_reason: This is an analytical statistical-mechanics study of two-layer student-teacher networks trained by one-pass SGD on Gaussian inputs with power-law covariance spectra, plus one linear student-teacher run on CIFAR-5m inputs labelled by a random teacher. It derives conditions under which squared-loss generalization error follows power laws in training time and in the number of trainable features. It does not measure held-out loss of language models, or of image or video models trained on real targets, so no version is tested. V5 names real models in other modalities and regimes, not toy networks with synthetic teachers. The results offer a theoretical mechanism for scaling laws and are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct, but it omits the plateau result. Fuller statement: in two-layer student-teacher networks with power-law data spectra, the authors derive conditions for power-law error scaling in training time (exponent β/(1+β)). They also derive a different exponent (β) for scaling with the number of trainable parameters or features. For erf activation, they give a formula showing that plateau length depends on the number of distinct eigenvalues and on hidden units. They find that convergence shifts from exponential to power-law under power-law spectra.
record.recipe_differences: Uses analytical statistical-mechanics and student-teacher methods, with one-pass SGD and squared-loss generalization error; it does not use language-model pretraining, held-out cross-entropy, or compute-optimal language-model sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: The temporal power-law regime is stated for small learning rates and a bounded time window; the nonlinear analysis also reports plateau behavior affected by the number of distinct covariance eigenvalues and hidden units.

fits_no_version.finding: In linear and erf two-layer student-teacher networks with a power-law input spectrum, generalization error decays as α^(−β/(1+β)) within a bounded time window. With an isotropic spectrum, convergence is exponential instead.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Power-law data covariance spectra are sufficient to produce power-law learning curves in training time in solvable two-layer networks trained by SGD.

fits_no_version.finding: The asymptotic error scales as Nl^−β in the number of trainable features. This exponent differs from the time exponent β/(1+β). The appendix reports the same exponent outside the covariance eigenbasis, with stated close agreement to simulation (Fig. 15).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Scaling exponents in time and in model size differ and are set by the data spectrum exponent in toy models.

fits_no_version.finding: Symmetric-plateau escape time scales as τesc ∼ M²/(ηL). The plateau shortens as the number of distinct eigenvalues grows and lengthens with more hidden units.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Plateau length in toy-network learning curves depends on data spectrum richness and network width.

record.problems: The results concern idealized two-layer student-teacher networks and squared-loss generalization error, not language models or held-out cross-entropy. The CIFAR-5m result is presented as a plot, and the text gives no uncertainty estimates for the reported averages.

untested.parts: All: no language-model pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
All: no fitting on small runs and predicting larger runs.
All: no comparison of architecture shapes at fixed parameter count.
All: no real image, video, repeated-data, fine-tuning or transfer models. Only toy student-teacher networks are studied.
All: no comparison of fitting choices or published laws for real models.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked all rows to V5 and labelled it supports or limits_scope. That is overturned: V5 concerns real models in other modalities and regimes, whereas this paper studies idealized toy networks with synthetic teachers. The results explain a possible mechanism for scaling laws rather than testing whether any version holds. The paper is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss of language models as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger language-model runs from power laws fitted to small runs.
Compute-optimal allocation between model parameters and training tokens.
Loss sensitivity to depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Video models, repeated data, fine-tuning, transfer, and other modalities or training regimes beyond the settings studied.
Downstream-task performance and its predictability from scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of published exponents or compute-optimal splits on fitting choices, and systematic bending away from a single power law.

rows.subject: two-layer linear student-teacher network
rows.size_stated: K = M = 1; input dimension N and number of distinct eigenvalues L
rows.operation_detail: Derives generalization error as a function of training time α for power-law data covariance spectra.
rows.value: The paper derives ϵg(α) ∝ α^(−β/(1+β)) within the stated time window.
rows.note: Analytical result for the stated student-teacher model and regime; it is not a language-model loss result.
rows.check: Analytical power law ϵg ∝ α^(−β/(1+β)) in a linear toy student-teacher model. Not the kind of system any version names, so it is unlinked from V5. The derived state is correct.

rows.subject: two-layer linear student-teacher network
rows.operation_detail: Simulates generalization error over training time and compares it with the analytical prediction.

conditions.value: synthetic Gaussian inputs with power-law spectrum

rows.note: The caption says the simulated error is compared with the analytical prediction but does not describe the degree of agreement.
rows.check: Synthetic-data simulation versus theory, shown only as a figure. Toy model, so unlinked from V5.

rows.subject: two-layer linear student-teacher network
rows.size_stated: L = N; Nl trainable input components, with Nl ≤ L = N
rows.operation_detail: Derives asymptotic generalization error as the number of trainable student features varies.
rows.measure: Asymptotic squared-loss generalization error versus Nl
rows.value: The paper gives ϵg,asymp ≈ [(1 + σJ²)λ+/(2βL)](1/L^β − 1/Nl^β), and states that the scaling with learned features is ϵg,asymp ∼ 1/Nl^β under the stated condition.
rows.note: This is a feature-count scaling result in a toy network, not a conventional language-model parameter-count sweep.
rows.check: Analytical feature-count scaling ϵg,asymp ∼ Nl^−β in a linear toy model, valid when L > Nl^β. Unlinked from V5.

rows.subject: two-layer linear student-teacher network trained on CIFAR-5m
rows.operation_detail: Varies trainable input dimension on the first channel of flattened CIFAR-5m images and compares simulation with the prediction.
rows.measure: Generalization error ϵg versus α for different Nl
rows.note: The caption reports comparison with the theoretical prediction using the empirical data spectrum; it does not state the degree of agreement in text.
rows.check: Uses CIFAR-5m inputs with a random linear teacher as the target. This is not an image model trained on real labels, so it does not bear on V5. The figure caption states no degree of agreement.

rows.subject: two-layer nonlinear student-teacher network
rows.stage_stated: one-pass stochastic gradient descent; feature-learning regime
rows.operation_detail: Studies asymptotic generalization-error convergence over training time with error-function activation.
rows.value: The paper states that all configurations show ϵg ∝ α^(−β/(1+β)) and that convergence shifts from exponential to power-law behavior for a power-law covariance spectrum.
rows.note: The stated power law is for asymptotic generalization error in the specified nonlinear student-teacher regime.
rows.check: Nonlinear (erf) toy student-teacher model. The paper states ϵg ∝ α^(−β/(1+β)) across five β values. Unlinked from V5.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Two-layer student-teacher networks with power-law covariance spectra, including the tested nonlinear feature-learning case
reader_labels.reason: The paper derives power-law generalization-error scaling with training time and learned features, and states the temporal exponent observed across the tested nonlinear configurations (r1, r3, r5).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
